source_refs.title: Delete apps on your iPhone or iPad - Apple Support
source_refs.section: How to delete an app; Before you get started; If you don't see the option to delete an app
source_refs.applicability: iPhone (the page covers iPhone and iPad); published September 14, 2026
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Touch and hold the app. Tap 'Remove App.' Tap 'Delete App,' then tap 'Delete' to confirm.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: Touch and hold the app. Tap 'Remove App.' Tap 'Delete App,' then tap 'Delete' to confirm. If you delete an app, it doesn't automatically cancel in-app subscriptions. If you don't see the option to delete an app, some built-in Apple apps can't be deleted. For third-party apps, check parental controls and make sure 'Deleting Apps' is set to 'Allow.' If an MDM solution manages the device, you may not be able to delete apps, so contact your administrator.

source_refs.title: Delete apps on your Android device - Google Play Help
source_refs.applicability: Android; the page says some of these steps work only on Android 13 and up
source_refs.verified_excerpt: At the top right, tap the Profile icon.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: Launch the Play Store app. Tap your profile icon in the top-right corner. Tap 'Manage apps & devices,' then tap 'Manage.' Select the app you want to remove. Tap 'Uninstall.' Some of these steps work only on Android 13 and up. Supervised users can use some Personal Safety app features.

source_refs.title: Uninstall or remove apps and programs in Windows | Microsoft Support
source_refs.section: Uninstall from the Start menu; Uninstall in Settings
source_refs.applicability: Windows 11 (the Applies To line lists Windows 10 and Windows 11)
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Press and hold (or right-click) on the app, then select Uninstall.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Windows 11: Open Start, go to 'All apps,' and search the list for the app. Press and hold the app, or right-click it, then choose 'Uninstall.' Open Start, then Settings, then Apps, then 'Installed apps.' Find the app, select 'More,' then choose 'Uninstall.' Some apps can't be uninstalled from the Settings app right now. For these, use the Control Panel method in the 'Uninstall from Control Panel' section. Apps built into Windows can't be uninstalled, so you may not see an Uninstall option for them.

source_refs.title: Delete or uninstall apps on Mac - Apple Support
source_refs.section: How to delete or uninstall an app on Mac
source_refs.verified_excerpt: If the app isn't made by Apple, find out whether it includes an 'Uninstall' or 'Uninstaller' app
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Mac: Quit the app first. If the app is currently open, quit the app before continuing. Locate it in the Applications folder, or use Spotlight with Command (⌘) and double-click. If the app isn't made by Apple, find out whether it includes an 'Uninstall' or 'Uninstaller' app. If the app doesn't include an uninstall app or feature, drag the app to the Trash. If you're asked for a user name and password, enter the name and password of an administrator account on your Mac. To permanently delete the app and make its storage space available for other items, choose Finder > Empty Trash. You can't use the Finder to delete apps that are required by your Mac. If you can't delete an app because your Mac says that it's in use, make sure that the app isn't open.
